$comment: P0-06 — the certified main-branch protection contract for BOTH Bizosto repositories.
This file is the machine-readable half of docs/security/p0-06-github-main-protection.md.
scripts/verify-github-main-protection.mjs reads it and fails closed when a LIVE GitHub
ruleset no longer guarantees what is recorded here.
Every invariant below is DIRECTIONAL: the live configuration may be stronger than the
record, never weaker. That is what makes the record a ratchet rather than a snapshot.
It holds no credential, and it does not assume one is unnecessary.
bizosto-website is PRIVATE and must stay that way; nextjs-boilerplate is public, which is
a pre-existing governance finding rather than an approval. Neither fact is what makes the
drift check credential-light: each repository is verified by a workflow running INSIDE it,
under that repository's own automatic job token, so no personal access token is needed and
no repository holds a credential for the other.
An anonymous read is NOT sufficient to certify. GitHub serves bypass_actors only to callers
with sufficient access to the ruleset, so an unprivileged read cannot tell an empty bypass
list from a withheld one - see ruleset.bypass_actors_unobservable in the verifier.
`applied` is the one field that is not an invariant. It records whether the certified
protection EXISTS on that repository yet. A repository with applied:false is an open
P0-06 gap and the live verifier fails on it — which is the point. The verifier also
looks for a matching ruleset anyway, so the day the owner applies it the check starts
evaluating the real thing instead of just reporting it missing.

$comment: THIS IS AN OPEN P0-06 CONTROL GAP, AND IT IS DELIBERATE.
The floor is the value the live ruleset may not drop below. The target is the value
P0-06 wants. They differ because the repository has exactly ONE account with any
access at all - lacreativodesign, the owner, admin - and that account is the author
of every pull request. GitHub does not let a pull request author approve their own
pull request, so raising the live count to 1 today would not add a review: it would
stop anything merging, including the pull request that would undo it.
So the count stays 0 until an independent reviewer exists. Closing the gap is a
two-step owner action, in this order, never the second alone:
1. grant a second human WRITE access to the repository;
2. set required_approving_review_count to 1 AND set certifiedFloor to 1 here.
gapOpen is what keeps step 2 honest. The certification test refuses to let gapOpen go
false while certifiedFloor is still 0, so the gap cannot be closed on paper alone.

THE RULESET CONTROL IS GREEN. TWO OTHER CONTROLS ARE NOT.
1. VISIBILITY — OPEN. This repository is currently PUBLIC. It was published so that the
ruleset could be created at all: GitHub Free serves rulesets on public repositories
only. That is a temporary expedient and NOT the target state. This repository holds
proprietary Bizosto marketing source and must end up PRIVATE.
expectedVisibility therefore stays "private", and the verifier reports the current
public state as repository.visibility DRIFT. That failure is correct and intended; it
must not be silenced by changing the expectation. The owner action is to upgrade the
account to GitHub Pro or higher, make the repository private, and then re-verify that
the ruleset survived the visibility change.
2. INDEPENDENT REVIEW — OPEN. See requiredApprovingReviewCount above.
Because rulesetId is now known, the verifier pins the read to that id rather than
discovering the ruleset by name. Name discovery remains only as the fallback for a
repository whose id has not been recorded yet.
